effects.name: aerialsunsetflyover
effects.description: First-person aerial view flying forward over a surreal alien landscape at ~40m altitude. The ground occupies ~65% of the frame, displaying sweeping bands of vibrant color — electric purples rolling into deep teals, volcanic oranges and lime greens — like psychedelic geological formations seen from above. Near terrain is crisp with visible FBM ridge detail and strong perspective convergence lines. By 150 virtual units distant, terrain colors wash toward warm cream-orange fog; by 300 units only silhouette shapes remain dissolved in haze. The horizon is completely washed out into a blindingly bright warm cream-orange atmospheric glow. Sky transitions from deep violet-indigo at the top through a magenta band narrowing into the horizon glow. A soft overexposed sun disc sits just above center-horizon, surrounded by a wide corona bloom and horizontal lens-streak artifacts. The camera breathes gently with a vertical Y-axis bob and lazy lateral banking. ALL animation uses sin(time*TAU) and cos(time*TAU) exclusively. Terrain forward motion is achieved by offsetting the FBM spatial coordinates using timeCircle = vec2(cos(time*TAU), sin(time*TAU)) scaled by speed — this traces a circle in the noise field giving seamless looping terrain scroll. Camera Y bob: sin(time*TAU)*2.5 (1 cycle). Banking: sin(time*TAU)*0.06 (1 cycle). Hue drift adds sin(time*TAU)*0.4 to cosine palette t-parameter. Sun Y oscillates with sin(time*TAU)*0.04. Lens flare pulse uses sin(time*TAU*2.0) (2 integer cycles). Post-processing: subtle chromatic aberration at screen edges, circular vignette, soft film grain from hash noise, sun corona/streak lens effects.
